column8: Sun 22 Nov: 3a's one parallel at source: the Lottery Commission's investment policy (reaffirmed 25 Sep 2025, s.III) quoted whole, with or as near prior as practicable; now the head row for the quote; cite the 2025 policy, never California law.
Sun 22 Nov: 3a, guards the parallel's label: Gov. Code 8880.25.5 only lets the Commission invest, so the rule is its investment policy, never California law or statute; one word in the citation.
Sun 22 Nov: store; which word the 19 Nov 2026 redline strikes is Keel's inference, so quote only the words unchanged in both versions and cite the September 2025 policy.

Sun 22 Nov: 3a, the words the old quote dropped are Caplet's own rule (TNA l.5: the latest WInS bond available beforehand; two of the ten end 231 and 320 days early, CANON B8), so one clause makes the parallel exact instead of flattering.
Sun 22 Nov: the policy's aim names reinvestment risk, but row 6 shows what it means (a call or a downgrade); alone it invites the false pairing with the extra Treasuries, so it travels with row 6.

Sun 22 Nov: 3a guard: the lottery's reinvestment risk is a call or downgrade on its municipal and agency bonds, while Laura's is the rate on interest waiting (TNA l.5), so never extra bonds against reinvestment risk as its precedent (ARGUMENT_TREE branch 2).
Sun 22 Nov: the policy ties the reserve bonds to its municipal bonds' credit and call risk, the same finding as row 8's audited credit-risk filing; travels with row 8.

Sun 22 Nov: 3a guard: the audited ACFR files the $2m par reserve under credit risk, which a fixed-income judge can find in one click; the reason Q16-020, Q31-010, Q28-014 and Q150-011 are corrected today.

Sun 22 Nov: store; fix before use: the lottery's 0.27% of par covers credit and call risk, not interest rates, so the thirty-times ratio sets two different spares side by side (Keel arithmetic); say only that zeros need no reinvestment spare at all (row 10), never this ratio.

Sun 22 Nov: 3a, the parallel's break read at source in the lottery's own ACFR (zero-coupon Treasuries, 83.0% of the 2025 book): a zero has nothing to reinvest, Laura may not hold STRIPS, so the extra Treasuries ($36,774, NUMBERS) are what the ban costs; upgrades Q31-010's inference, beside Q17-010.

Sun 22 Nov: 3a or 3e, one checkable sentence from the same body as the parallel (no interest rate policy because the investments mirror the payments); a twin of Washington's Q73-007, so one of the two.
Sun 22 Nov: store; the lottery's Buy and Hold keeps an exit for gain, which IPS l.17 does not, a contrast for a judge's question, never a second parallel.
Sun 22 Nov: store; the exit was used once, in the 2008-10 budget crisis (about $61.4m, Keel arithmetic); the link to the municipal bonds and the reserve is UNVERIFIED.

Sun 22 Nov: 3a colour inside the one parallel: the lottery buys its Treasuries when the promise is made, timed to its dates, which is Laura's order; fully funded is the lottery's word, never full funding for the facility.
Sun 22 Nov: store; continuous appropriation is why California never had Illinois's 2015 problem; Laura has no appropriation step, so nothing for the report.

Sun 22 Nov: store or Table 3's custody note: a state holds its Treasuries through a commercial bank too, so Laura's broker and custodian chain is the normal one (card Q72); uninsured is the GASB label, never a risk claim.
Sun 22 Nov: store; the 1984 law left the instrument open and the policy chose Treasuries, as the IPS did; no part needs it.
Sun 22 Nov: 3a or 2.2, one clause inside the one parallel: Mega Millions sets its payment dates by the bonds, while the case fixes Laura's each January, which is why two of her ten end months early.
Sun 22 Nov: store; many sellers, one payer who owns the bonds; the co-sponsor reading is a stretch, since co-sponsors never fund the ten (case l.91-93).
Sun 22 Nov: store detail; Powerball's 5% graduation is not Laura's flat schedule (case l.90); not for the report.
Sun 22 Nov: store, beside row 8: no lottery reserve read is held against interest rates, because none holds coupon bonds for its prizes.

Sun 22 Nov: store or a 3a reserve: Illinois keeps its Treasury-funded prizes in a trust fund with an irrevocable appropriation, the public form of the two pots; 3a's one parallel is the lottery rule and its funders' reason is Oman's, so a second outside voice would break D6.
Sun 22 Nov: the other half of row 22's structure (cash prizes wait on appropriations and may not pay deferred winners); travels with row 22.
Sun 22 Nov: store; the 2015 freeze stopped the appropriated pot while the trust fund paid $37.0m in the year; installment winners paid on time is Keel's inference, never stated as fact.
Sun 22 Nov: store; the dated chain of 2015 beside Q2b-006's count; no part needs the dates.
Sun 22 Nov: store; the plainest words for money present and authority missing; Laura needs no authority to pay, so colour only.
Sun 22 Nov: adds the court's own words to Q2b-007's dismissal; no part needs them.

Sun 22 Nov: store; a public payer may be barred from funding next year's promises with this year's money and a private one is not, so the IPS's buy-first order is open to Laura; a judge's-question note.
Sun 22 Nov: a think tank's one-line correction (money against authority); cite the statute in row 22 instead.

Sun 22 Nov: store; FINRA 2165 holds apply only at 65 or older or impaired, with exploitation suspected (the case gives no age), so at most a set-up note (a trusted contact), never a reason to change the plan (IPS l.17).

Sun 22 Nov: 3e, at most a clause beside the broker-failure delay already listed: every route to a late payment with the money present is delay, not loss, and none waits on anyone's vote; a Keel combination.
Sun 22 Nov: store; a public payer calls Treasuries free from credit risk with no qualifier, support for Book 19's strong words; its 89.4% AAA covers agencies and munis, never AAA for the US (D20).

Sun 22 Nov: 3c's parallel with its citation fixed: the RBA's Review of its approach to forward guidance (15 Nov 2022), section 3, p.14 (page inferred), never its 2022 review; the quote itself is Q94-002's.
Sun 22 Nov: three RBA reviews in 2022 and only November's says promise: the reason row 1 names the document; travels with it.

Sun 22 Nov: 3c, a clause at most inside the RBA parallel: its June 2022 review calls time-based guidance conditional by nature and a dated-bond target a commitment to that date; the break (a price defended along the way, row 13) comes with it.

Sun 22 Nov: 3c, with 3d's pledge letter in view (aha A): the Governor refused the word pledge and gave a best guess with a high degree of confidence, and the public heard a pledge; Laura signs one only once Treasuries held for her will pay it; never pledge in the report's own voice.
Sun 22 Nov: 3c, judge's note B in the official Hansard: the text was conditional and right and was still heard as 2024; strengthens Q94-010's interview, one clause at most.
Sun 22 Nov: 3c or 3d colour: the official Hansard words that replace Q94-012's news version (the community heard 2024, not the conditionality); quote these only.
Sun 22 Nov: store; the Board said its date was computable from published material, so a computed figure said aloud became a promise; a judge's-question note for 3c.
Sun 22 Nov: store; the RBA traded true for clear on purpose; after the move Laura's one figure is both, which 3c already says.
Sun 22 Nov: 3c beside aha 7: two softenings did not move the anchor, so the first figure said is the one kept and must already be paid for; one clause inside the RBA parallel at most.

Sun 22 Nov: 3c beside aha 7: six months out the Governor called a 2022 rise extremely unlikely; NUMBERS 4's 8.6% (6 months) and 10.6% (12 months) are quoted right; the disanalogy (a whole economy against one fund's price) goes with it.

Sun 22 Nov: 3c and 3d's no-caveat rule: the independent Review (2023, p.62) ruled that public messages cannot rely on detailed caveats, overruling the Bank's own cure; extends Q94-016's p.52; one clause.
Sun 22 Nov: store; listeners lean on the speaker's figure, and the Review's word credibility matches the case's own (case l.114); support only.

Sun 22 Nov: 3c, a clause at most: the RBA's dated target broke because it promised a price along the way (it held about 60% of the bond), while Laura's figure is what a dated fund pays at its end; the payout is not fixed (D2), so the margin goes with it.

Sun 22 Nov: 3c and D12: before the move publish the rule and the risks, not the figure, so the residency's planners hear the held bottom and no co-sponsor hears a top; the quotes repeat Q94-008, the application is new.

Sun 22 Nov: 3c, the parallel's break in one line of reasoning: before the move she stands where the RBA stood, after it where no central bank can; a Keel synthesis, and nothing left to forecast is true while no condition at all is not (NUMBERS 8u).
Sun 22 Nov: store vocabulary: the profession says market implied, the word the report uses for forward rates (Q205); never evidence that forwards forecast well.
Sun 22 Nov: store; the SNB's 2011 words were as hard as words get; the RBA's companion for a judge's question, never a second parallel in 3c (D6).
Sun 22 Nov: store; reaffirmed 28 days before it ended (Keel arithmetic); determination restated is not money set aside.
Sun 22 Nov: store; temporary appeared only on the day the floor ended, while the IPS writes its two exits at the start (IPS l.17).
Sun 22 Nov: store; an open-ended promise cannot be exited in public; Laura's held figure needs no defence, so her rules can be public from the start.

Sun 22 Nov: store; fix the use: no further money is needed at today's market rates, but an early end of the late-2032 fund with waiting cash at zero could leave the top up to $4,589 short, met from her flexibility (NUMBERS 3), so never no further money is ever needed.
Sun 22 Nov: the SNB's break is row 13's (a promise kept by defending a price, not by holding to a payout); travels with row 13.
Sun 22 Nov: store; the SNB's own hindsight that waiting would have cost more; no part needs it.

Sun 22 Nov: store; the Fed's at-least dates held by circumstance (Q94-019 has the moves); fix the use: never a top that can only be beaten, since the contribution is the lower of what the funds pay and the top, and an early fund end at zero interest can leave the top short (NUMBERS 3, 4).
Sun 22 Nov: store; the Fed wrote both directions down and the RBA did not; the upside reading breaks for Laura (Q94-006's note), so store only.

Sun 22 Nov: store; the Bank of Canada backed its 2009 date in part with term lending, the nearest a central bank came to holding its figure; the 6 May speaker is unchecked; conceit words never in tables.

Sun 22 Nov: store; fix the use: never nothing she states can change (an early fund end at zero interest, NUMBERS 3); say nothing she states waits on a later market price, so no public withdrawal is planned.
Sun 22 Nov: 3c judge's-question ladder (say less, back the words partly with money, speak once held); a Keel ranking, never a source's.

Sun 22 Nov: 3c, the parallel's sentence accurate to the source (February 2021's until 2024 at the earliest; the November 2022 review's a promise), as ARGUMENT_TREE branch 4 now carries it; the writers recast it in Caplet's voice.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e's one parallel: the Bank's own words for who was hit (came under particular pressure; pooled funds' lags and many small investors), which replace broke fastest (ARGUMENT_TREE branch 6).
Sun 22 Nov: store; the Bank's word is prospect: its purchases came before the forced sales it feared, so nothing broke.
Sun 22 Nov: 3e, the sourced phrase forced sellers (Bailey, HC 826 para 50) for the parallel's first clause; row 1 is the primary citation.
Sun 22 Nov: 3e, the mechanism under pooled funds above all: limited liability let investors decline to pay in, while no fund she holds ever asks her, or anyone holding beside her, to pay in.
Sun 22 Nov: Parliament's summary that smaller schemes in pooled funds came off worst repeats row 1's Bank finding.
Sun 22 Nov: 3e reserve detail: funds came within a morning of winding up and none did, the fact a UK bond judge will not expect; never broke or collapsed.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e and Table 3 row 4: decisions made on pooled investors' behalf have one counterpart for Laura, a sponsor's early end paid at net asset value (NUMBERS 3: at most $4,589 short of the top if waiting cash earns nothing), which is why nobody can make the plan sell fails.
Sun 22 Nov: store; calls ran on a five-day clock and recapitalisation on a week-plus one; Laura has no call and so no clock.

Sun 22 Nov: store; fix the use: nothing Laura holds is pledged to a lender, but her funds may lend up to a third of their Treasuries against collateral (Q26-015, Q65-031), so never every Treasury held for her is unencumbered.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e, the measurement under the parallel: firms with more gilt repo sold more (R squared 0.56 against 0.17 for swaps), so funding that could be called was the variable, and hers is zero; a staff working paper, cited as such.
Sun 22 Nov: 3e wording guard: segregated mandates were 85-90% of the market and also sold, so pooled funds above all says who was forced, never who sold most.
Sun 22 Nov: store; the 2022 storm missed short gilts, and by 2031 the late-2032 fund is short; one UK episode promises nothing about 2031.
Sun 22 Nov: Table 3 row 5's job: bystanders' small trades got dearer without being forced, which the 0.5% trade-day limit answers; one clause at most.
Sun 22 Nov: store; the Bank's own pairing of 2022 with March 2020 (more than twice the previous record, Q2a-001's sentence) plus Pinter's 2-3 times the LDI sales; background for row 32.
Sun 22 Nov: store; the patient side gained (the Bank resold at a 3.8bn pound profit, read at one remove); Laura is never the forced seller.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e's parallel, the true narrow replacement for no pension promise broke: no scheme became insolvent and the PPF saw no claim from the episode, by November 2022; never every member was paid.
Sun 22 Nov: 3e's disanalogy in the insurer's words: no DB scheme ran short of assets, it was the speed and form of collateral calls; Laura owes no call, in any form, at any speed.
Sun 22 Nov: the regulator's hedged line (significantly, short-term) backs row 16's narrow sentence; use row 16.
Sun 22 Nov: 3e guard: over 2022 most schemes' funding improved and about 5% both worsened and went into or deeper into deficit (TPR model), the honest size behind never no pension promise broke.
Sun 22 Nov: store guard: the 5% were schemes hedged beyond their assets, and the equities-then-gilts order is the regulator's assumption, never a finding.
Sun 22 Nov: store guard: no count of losers exists (TPR, the Minister), so never every member was paid; the Committee and Minister mismatch stays in the critique.
Sun 22 Nov: 3e, one clause at most: every route to a loss in 2022 ran through a call for cash (a hedge cut, a sale low, a loan from the employer), and Laura has none of the three.
Sun 22 Nov: store; fix the use: the half kept is never sold to meet a call, but it is hers to spend on IPS l.15's uses, so drop never sold to meet anything.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e, an aha candidate inside the parallel: borrowing turned the longest-horizon investor into one of the shortest; Laura's horizon stays her payment dates because nothing she holds asks her to make good; critics' words, so pair them with Breeden's.
Sun 22 Nov: store; the FPC pairs 2020 and 2022 and warns against relying on rescue; the plan relies on none.
Sun 22 Nov: store companion: March 2020's forced sellers were leveraged basis traders and holders needing dollars; never a second parallel in 3e (D6).
Sun 22 Nov: store; in March 2020 funds holding only US government securities took inflows; not iBond funds, and bills, not 2032 bonds.
Sun 22 Nov: Table 3 row 5's basis or one clause: the Fed names mismatch and leverage as March 2020's two causes, and the plan has neither.
Sun 22 Nov: 3e and Table 3 row 5: a Treasury ETF's price can sit below its value in a stress and come back (TLT's average gap 0.13% to 0.86%); a price, not a call, so her one planned sale waits.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e's corrected claim (no price can make her sell; a date can), kept; fix one figure: a fill at the 0.5% limit on every leg leaves $95,000 and $115,000 unchanged only centrally; in the house model the two range legs lower the bottom a step in 10.0% of paths and the top in 14.0% (NUMBERS 4).
Sun 22 Nov: 3e, a clause at most: her funds share a pool of Treasuries, never a debt, so 2022's pooled-fund trap cannot form; the fund half rests on Q36 and Q3c.
Sun 22 Nov: placement, adopted in ARGUMENT_TREE branch 6: March 2020 belongs in Table 3 row 5's 0.5% basis or one clause, never as 3e's second parallel.

Sun 22 Nov: 3a's one parallel, corrected by card Q211 rows 1, 2 and 4: name it the Lottery Commission's investment policy (reaffirmed 25 Sep 2025, s.III), never California law; quote it whole with or as near prior as practicable (this row's note cut it to immediately prior), never exactly; Q211-001 is now the head row at source.

Sun 22 Nov: store; corrected by card Q211 rows 6-8: the quote stands, but the lottery's reinvestment risk is a call or downgrade on its municipal and agency bonds and its $2m par reserve is filed under credit risk, so never a precedent for the extra Treasuries; the true contrast is zeros against coupons (Q211 row 10); the $21,149 margin is an old figure (extra Treasuries now $36,774).

Sun 22 Nov: store; corrected by card Q211 rows 6-10: the 2024 size stands, but the reserve covers calls and downgrades and is filed under credit risk, never a spare pot for reinvestment risk or a twin of the backstop; the STRIPS reading is now read at source (row 10); the forty-times ratio and $45,456 of $444,545 are old (row 9; NUMBERS 8h now $46,566 of $445,655).

Sun 22 Nov: store and exhibits; corrected by card Q211 rows 6-8: sufficiency shown in a sentence and a par table stands (Q16-022's point), but the reserve is filed under credit risk, against calls and downgrades on municipal bonds, never the role of Caplet's backstop or the extra Treasuries.

Sun 22 Nov: refused: SB-8's one new link is false, since a lottery's reserve bonds cover credit risk and calls and its zeros leave no interest on interest to cover (card Q211 rows 6-8, 10), so the extra Treasuries do not sit as a lottery's reserve bonds do; the rest is NUMBERS 8a's 3% to about 15% (NUM-002).

Sun 22 Nov: 3c, aha 7's speaking early; corrected per card Q212 Gaps: a top stated 12 months early means the move would buy less than it in 10.6% of house paths (NUMBERS 4 since 17 Nov; 10.7% void), never not yet owned in; and a stated top is held in Treasuries that will pay it, never already owned (ATTACKS D2).

Sun 22 Nov: 3c or 3d colour; card Q212 row 6 read the official Hansard of 28 Nov 2022, so quote its words (The community heard 2024; they didn't hear the conditionality, and that's partly our fault), never this row's news versions (a failure on our part); the ABC loan count stays out.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d and 3e; corrected per card Q212 Gaps: holding the figure in Treasuries that will pay it protects her later asks, never owning the figure (ATTACKS D2); Q212 rows 12 and 23 add the Review's and the SNB's words on credibility.

Sun 22 Nov: store; corrected per card Q212 Gaps: certain because Treasuries held for her will pay it, never because she owns it (ATTACKS D2); Q212 rows 3 and 13 now carry the yield-target lesson with its break (a price defended along the way, not a payout at a fund's end).
Sun 22 Nov: store; corrected per card Q212 Gaps: a figure that Treasuries held for her will pay makes both readings true, never an owned figure (ATTACKS D2).

Sun 22 Nov: 3c; corrected per card Q212 Gaps: a three-year commitment with no conditions is unwise unless Treasuries held for her already pay it, never unless the money is owned (ATTACKS D2); Woodford argues for better commitment, not against it.

Sun 22 Nov: a 27 Nov check for 3d's sentence; corrected per card Q212 Gaps: it is a commitment because Treasuries held for her will pay it and a signed pledge letter makes it countable (card Q200), never because it is owned (ATTACKS D2); the feature's authors are still unchecked for APA.

Sun 22 Nov: 3c or Table 2's note; corrected per card Q212 Gaps and row 14: co-sponsors hear only a figure that Treasuries held for her will pay, never the owned figure (ATTACKS D2), and from January 2028 the residency's planners may hear the held bottom (D12).
Sun 22 Nov: store; corrected per card Q212 Gaps: a precise figure that Treasuries held for her will already pay, never one already owned (ATTACKS D2).

Sun 22 Nov: 3c's reason in notes; corrected per card Q212 Gaps: the four shares are 2.9%, 6.2%, 8.6% and 10.6%, said as the move would buy less than the stated top (NUMBERS 4, 17 Nov), never not yet owned in; she states only figures Treasuries held for her will pay, never figures she owns (ATTACKS D2); earlier fixes stand.

Sun 22 Nov: store; corrected per card Q212 Gaps: ink is a figure that Treasuries held for her will pay, never one that is hers or owned (ATTACKS D2); 3c's turn is now two inkings, two dates (ARGUMENT_TREE branch 4) and let the ink dry is retired, so this candidate is superseded.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e's one parallel, corrected by card Q214: never broke fastest (no LDI fund wound up; the sources say came under particular pressure and forced sellers, rows 1, 3, 6) and never no pension promise broke (a minority ended worse funded, rows 19, 21); say the funds forced to sell had borrowed against their gilts, pooled funds above all, and no scheme became insolvent and the PPF saw no claim by November 2022 (rows 4, 16).

Sun 22 Nov: 3e wording, corrected by card Q214: never the promises held (row 16's narrower form: no scheme became insolvent and the PPF saw no claim by November 2022; about 5% of schemes ended worse funded, rows 19, 21); no lender and no depositor can make Laura sell stays, said as no price can make her sell, since a fund sponsor's early end can turn a holding into cash (rows 7, 30); the earlier fixes stand.

Sun 22 Nov: 2.0 or 3b's design not taken, one clause; corrected by card Q214 rows 7 and 30: check (3) reads no price and no lender can force a sale before the date, never nothing can, since a sponsor's early end of IBTM pays its value in cash (Table 3 row 4; NUMBERS 3, at most $4,589 short of the top if waiting cash earns nothing); the floor passes it in that form.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e, collateral calls come from falls in value; corrected by card Q214 rows 7 and 30: the clause it supports is no price can force a sale, never nobody can (a fund sponsor's early end can, and she can choose to sell); the speaker has a motive.

Sun 22 Nov: store, Orange County never named in the report; corrected by card Q214 rows 7 and 30: the lesson unnamed is that a forced seller sells at the bottom and no price can force Laura to sell, never nothing can (a fund sponsor's early end; her own choice); the road-money line stays overstated (W-05).

Sun 22 Nov: store only, Orange County never named; corrected by card Q214 rows 7 and 30: the test it sets is ability to hold, said for Laura as no price and no lender can force a sale (she borrows nothing, pledges nothing, owes no cash on demand), never no one can (a fund sponsor's early end; her own choice).

Sun 22 Nov: 3e beside Figure 1, the forced-seller warning is common pension practice; corrected by card Q214 rows 7 and 30: say no price can force a sale, never no one can (a fund sponsor's early end pays net asset value on the sponsor's date).
